extracted.intended_audience: members, officers, directors, and prospective members of the National Association of Science Writers (NASW)
extracted.subtask_description: Formal constitution and bylaws governing membership classes, rights, meetings, board composition and procedures, officer duties, disciplinary processes, conflict-of-interest rules, financial reporting, and amendment procedures for the National Association of Science Writers, Inc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name of organization
rubrics_metrics.description: This organization shall be known as the National Association of Science Writers, Inc. (the "Association" or "NASW").

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Foster the dissemination of accurate information regarding science and technology through all media normally devoted to informing the public; foster interpretation of science and its meaning to society, in keeping with the highest standards of journalism; and foster and promote the professional interests of science writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classes of membership
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be four classes of membership in the Association: Professional, Honorary, Affiliate and Student. References to 'members' or the 'membership' shall mean Professional members unless otherwise specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for professional membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional members shall be people who are professional science writers or instructors of science writing, including — but not limited to — journalists, authors, editors, producers, public information officers, and people who write and produce films, audio, museum exhibits and programs, and other material intended to inform the public about science and technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for honorary membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Honorary membership may be extended to those who have notably aided the purposes of the organization as expressed in Article I, Section 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for student membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Student members shall be enrolled in a school or degree program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for affiliate membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiliate Members shall be individuals who have a strong personal interest in science writing as a profession and who uphold the aims and mission of the organization and who do not fit into one of the other classes; Affiliate members shall meet any other requirements set by Board resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting rights by class
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional members shall have full voting privileges. Student members, Affiliate members and Honorary members may not vote or hold office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member of record for at least six months preceding their demand has the right to examine minutes of proceedings and list or record of members and to make copies, during usual business hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection may be denied if the member refuses to furnish an affidavit that the inspection will not be used for purposes other than the business of the Association and has not within five years given or offered for sale any list of members or aided others in procuring such lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual meeting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Association shall have an annual meeting of members at a time and place designated by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may also designate other regular meetings of members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special meetings of members
rubrics_metrics.description: Special meetings may be called at the direction of the Board or president; a group of at least 10 percent of the members may petition the secretary to call a special meeting (to be held not less than two months nor more than three months following the petition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If secretary fails to give notice within five business days after receiving a petition, any member signing the petition may give notice. Special meeting notice must state the purpose(s) for which the meeting is called. If there is a failure to elect sufficient directors under certain timelines, provisions of Section 604 of the New York N-PCL apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of membership meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary must give written notice stating place, date and hour of membership meetings: (a) personally, first-class mail, facsimile or e-mail at least 10 days but no more than 50 days in advance; or (b) by other class of mail at least 30 days but no more than 60 days in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If mailed, notice is given when deposited with prepaid postage to the member's address on record or other address filed; electronic or fax notice is given when directed to the member's recorded fax or e-mail. Electronic notice is not deemed given if two consecutive notices cannot be delivered or Association otherwise knows notice cannot be delivered electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quorum for member meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Members entitled to cast 100 votes or 10 percent of the total number of votes entitled to be cast, whichever is less, shall constitute a quorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting rules for members
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where otherwise specified, (a) all actions of the Association shall be determined by the Board, and (b) corporate action by members (other than election of directors) shall be authorized by a majority of the votes cast at a meeting with a quorum present. Members may cast their vote by proxy in elections of directors or officers or for other matters specified by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board manages the Association
rubrics_metrics.description: The Association shall be managed by its Board of Directors (the 'Board').

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and qualifications of directors
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to four ex officio directors, the Board shall consist of 11 Board members at large. Any Professional Association member at least 18 years old is eligible to serve as a Board member. 'Entire Board' means 15 directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of office for at-large directors
rubrics_metrics.description: All at-large Board members shall serve for two years commencing no more than 4 months following their election and until a successor director has been elected and qualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination process for at-large directors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nominating Committee shall nominate at least 15 members to run for at-large seats. A group of 20 or more members may nominate by petition; nominees must meet requirements in Article III Section 2. All nominations shall be forwarded to the executive director no less than 6 months prior to the end of current Board members' terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of at-large directors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will set timing of biennial NASW elections of Board members at-large within six months prior to an annual meeting. The executive director shall prepare and send a proxy form reflecting all conforming nominations. Board members shall be elected at an annual meeting by a plurality of votes cast, if a quorum is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filling Board vacancies and removal
rubrics_metrics.description: A vacancy exists upon death, resignation, removal, or increase in authorized number of directors. Any director may be removed with cause by vote of members or directors at a duly held meeting. Vacancies shall be filled by vote of the members at a regular or special meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place and notice of Board meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Board meetings may be held at any place within or outside New York designated by the Board. Regular meetings may be held without notice on dates fixed by the Board. Special Board meetings may be called by the President or by any director upon written demand of at least one-fifth of the entire Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of special meetings shall be sent at least four days before the meeting by e-mail or first-class mail (or by facsimile); for matters requiring prompt action, notice may be given no less than forty-eight hours before the meeting and may be by personal delivery, telephone, e-mail or facsimile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of notice for Directors
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice need not be given to any Director who submits a waiver of notice (before or after the meeting) or who attends without protesting lack of notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver may be written or electronic. Written waiver must be signed (including by facsimile); electronic waiver must be an e-mail transmission with information to reasonably determine authorization by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board quorum and voting
rubrics_metrics.description: A majority of the entire Board constitutes a quorum for transaction of business. Unless otherwise provided, the vote of a majority of directors present at the time of a vote (if a quorum is present) is the act of the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directors present at a meeting who are not present at the time of a vote due to conflict of interest or related party transaction shall be determined to be present for purposes of calculating a quorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in meetings by conference telephone/video
rubrics_metrics.description: Board members not physically present may participate by conference telephone or similar communications equipment or electronic video screen communication. Participation by such means constitutes presence in person if all persons can hear each other at the same time and each director can participate in all matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action without meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Any action required or permitted to be taken by the Board may be taken without a meeting if all members consent to adoption of a resolution authorizing the action in writing or electronically. The resolution and written consents must be filed with the minutes of the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjournment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A majority of directors present, whether or not a quorum, may adjourn any meeting of the Board to another time and place. If adjourned for more than 24 hours, notice of adjournment shall be given prior to the adjourned meeting to directors who were not present at the time of adjournment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board committees: creation, composition, authority limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Bylaws or the Board may create one or more Board committees of three or more directors (no non-directors) to serve at the Board's pleasure. Appointments are by majority vote of the entire Board. A committee has all Board authority to the extent provided in the Board resolution or Bylaws, except that no committee shall have authority over certain matters (e.g., submission to members of actions requiring members' approval; filling Board vacancies; fixing director compensation; amending bylaws; amending certain Board resolutions) as specified or by Section 712(a) of the N-PCL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may appoint alternate directors to committees who replace absent members. Committee powers and limits must be set by resolution or Bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Committee, composed of the four ex officio directors, shall have the power to act in place of the Board between Board meetings on routine corporate matters, except as otherwise provided in Section 15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Board (corporate) committees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may create non-Board committees of the corporation; the Board appoints initial members and thereafter each such committee elects its members by majority vote. Members of such committees may be directors and/or non-directors. Such committees have authority as designated by the Board but are not committees of the Board and shall not exercise Board powers or bind the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice and procedures for such committees are prescribed by the committee chairman; meetings may be called by the President or committee chairman.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officers and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Elected officers are president, vice-president who is president-elect, treasurer, and secretary, who shall all be ex officio directors. A substantial majority of an officer's science-writing activities shall be journalism. Officers may not write press releases or otherwise act on behalf of an institution or company to affect media coverage while they serve in office; officers who engage in such activities must notify the Board immediately. No employee of the Association shall serve as President unless permitted under Section 713 of the N-PCL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an officer engages in disallowed activities, they may remain on the Board but the Board shall appoint another fully qualified member to carry out officer duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination and election process for officers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nominating Committee shall nominate one member for vice-president/president-elect, one for secretary, and one for treasurer. Membership and nominating committees may request material from candidates to identify qualifications. A group of 20+ members may nominate by petition. All nominations shall be forwarded to the executive director no less than six months prior to the end of the current officer's term. Officers shall be elected by a vote of the members; vacancies may be filled by majority vote of Board members then in office or by members at a regular or special meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Membership Committee determines whether nominees meet qualifications for officer (substantial majority journalism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of office for officers
rubrics_metrics.description: All officers shall serve for two years following their election and until a successor is elected and qualified; each vice-president shall serve two years as vice-president and then two years as president (total four years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of the President
rubrics_metrics.description: Preside over all meetings of the Association; call special meetings when advisable; call attention to developments threatening the organization or methods of improvement; appoint Nominating Committee; arrange for participation of the Association in other meetings and conferences as needed; represent the Association or arrange for representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of the Vice-President
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume the functions of the president when the president is unable or delegates them; serve as president-elect and assume the presidency when the president completes term or leaves office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of the Secretary
rubrics_metrics.description: Record proceedings of all meetings of the Association and provide each Board member with a copy of minutes of any Board meeting within one month after such meeting; write a summary of the annual meeting and any other meeting of the members to be circulated and filed as the minutes of a meeting of the members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of the Treasurer
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan an annual budget to be considered by the Board; transmit to the membership an annual summary of the financial status of the Association, as further described in Article X, Section 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership application review process
rubrics_metrics.description: A Membership Committee shall judge all classes of membership applications whenever questions arise about an applicant's qualifications. If the committee rejects an applicant, it shall inform the candidate of the reason. Decisions of the Membership Committee may be appealed to the Executive Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of honorary members
rubrics_metrics.description: Honorary members, nominated by the Board or by petition signed by no fewer than 20 members, shall be elected by the members at a regular meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dues-setting authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership dues for all classes shall be fixed from time to time by vote of the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrears and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A member whose dues remain unpaid by February 28 shall be considered in arrears. A member in arrears shall have all services suspended and may not vote until dues and applicable fees are paid in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and termination for prolonged nonpayment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member who remains in arrears regarding dues for 12 months shall be given 30 days' notice that membership will be terminated if dues are not paid at the end of the 30-day period; the executive director shall give delinquent members notice by any method reasonably calculated to provide actual notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for termination of membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership terminates on resignation; expiration of membership unless renewed; failure to pay dues/fees within the 30-day notice period; or conduct substantially prejudicial to the purposes and interests of the Association (as determined under Section 4 of Article VII).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantially prejudicial conduct may include actions contrary to NASW’s Code of Ethics, Operating Principles, or Meeting and Conference Code of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of members
rubrics_metrics.description: A member of any class may be suspended or have certain privileges revoked for a limited time for conduct substantially prejudicial to the purposes and interests of the Association, as determined under the disciplinary procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing Ethics Committee and complaint intake
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall appoint a Standing Ethics Committee at the start of each fiscal year to act on complaints concerning NASW members. No member of the Standing Ethics Committee shall be a current Board member. A signed, written complaint may be delivered to the Executive Director or any Board member by a Reporter who believes in good faith that a member's conduct is substantially prejudicial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict screening and Review Committee formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receiving a complaint, the Administrator shall determine whether any relationship exists that could reasonably be expected to impair the ability to review the complaint. The Administrator forwards the complaint to Board members who are not Conflicted Members. The Board shall appoint a minimum of three members to a Review Committee composed of current Board members and Standing Ethics Committee members, with a majority of Standing Ethics Committee members; no Conflicted Member may serve on the Review Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Review Committee is a Committee of the Corporation as described in Article III Section 16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation threshold and process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Review Committee shall undertake a preliminary investigation to determine merit. If it determines the complaint has merit, it shall recommend a full investigation to the Board. Upon Board approval, the Review Committee shall proceed with a full investigation. Investigation details are spelled out in Standing Ethics and Review Committee Policies and Procedures and may include consulting the Subject and others, collecting evidence, consulting legal counsel, etc.; but the Review Committee shall not, without prior Board approval, enter material contracts, initiate communications with law enforcement/government authorities, or engage in activities that materially impact NASW or expose it to material financial or legal liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints will be handled with sensitivity and discretion and remain confidential to the extent permitted by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vote to proceed and Notice of Complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the full investigation, the Review Committee shall vote whether to proceed. An affirmative majority is required. If proceeding, the Committee shall provide the Board (excluding Conflicted Members) a draft Notice of Complaint with sufficient detail for the Subject to mount a defense. If the Board approves, it shall send the Notice to the Subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response, hearing, and Board sanction vote
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receiving Notice of Complaint, the Subject may submit a formal written response or schedule a hearing. After hearing or receipt of response (or if Subject does not respond or request hearing within 30 days after good-faith contact efforts), the Board will discuss and vote on a proposed sanction. An affirmative vote by no fewer than two-thirds of the Board members present and not Conflicted Members (if a quorum is present) is required to sanction or terminate membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board must notify the Subject of its decision and any sanctions (Notice of Decision) within 14 days of the hearing, receipt of Response, or close of the 30-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal process for sanctioned members
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon Notice of Decision, the Subject has 14 days to appeal in writing to the Review Committee with reasons for the appeal, which must include new evidence or extenuating circumstances. If appealed, the Review Committee will investigate and make a recommendation to the Board within 14 days of receipt of the appeal. The Board may amend or remove sanctions only by affirmative vote of no fewer than two-thirds of Board members present and not Conflicted Members. The Board shall notify the Subject of the decision on appeal within 14 days; the Board's decision on appeal is final and takes effect immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints by non-members
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints by non-members about a member's conduct shall be directed to the Executive Director or any Board member. The Executive Director or Board member shall determine, in consultation with the Board and Standing Ethics Committee (excluding Conflicted Members), whether to initiate any or all of the disciplinary procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whistleblower policy interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: NASW maintains a Whistleblower Policy for reports of suspected fraudulent or dishonest use/misuse of NASW resources by staff, officers, Board members, consultants, or volunteers. Such reports must be made pursuant to that policy and are not covered by the disciplinary procedures in Section 4; however, if corrective action under the Whistleblower Policy would include sanctioning or terminating a member, the disciplinary procedures of Section 4 must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for related party transactions and key persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'related party transaction' (any transaction where a related party has a financial interest and the Association is a participant); 'related party' (i) any Director, Officer or key person; (ii) a relative of such individuals; (iii) entities where such individuals have specified ownership interests; 'key person' has specified control/management influence; 'relative' defined by family relationships; 'substantial financial interest' is one determined by the Board/authorized committee to be significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other terms have meanings assigned in Section 102(a) of the N-PCL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for related party transactions (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before entering any related party transaction: (a) the Director, Officer, or key person with an interest must disclose that interest in good faith to the Board or authorized committee and the material facts; (b) no related party may participate in deliberations or voting on the transaction, though the Board may request background information from them before deliberation; (c) the Board or authorized committee must determine the transaction is fair, reasonable, and in the Association's best interest; and (d) contemporaneously document in writing the basis for approval, including consideration of any alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional procedures for transactions with substantial financial interest
rubrics_metrics.description: For related party transactions in which a related party has a substantial financial interest, in addition to the general procedures the Board or authorized committee must: (a) consider alternative transactions to the extent available, determine the transaction is fair, reasonable, and in the Association’s best interest, and approve by not less than a majority vote of directors or committee members present; and (b) contemporaneously document in writing the basis for approval including consideration of alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest policy maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Corporation shall maintain a Conflict of Interest Policy that complies with the requirements of applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment proposal and adoption procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment may be proposed by vote of three-fourths of the members present at a regular meeting or by vote of the Board. The proposed amendment shall be circulated to the membership and put to a vote at the next annual meeting (or other meeting if Board determines) and adopted if approved by a majority of members voting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment may also be proposed by petition of no less than 5 percent of members based on membership on the last March 1 preceding the petition; timelines apply (90 days in advance) and thresholds for reconsideration are specified if a proposal fails once or twice. The Board or Governance Committee will determine substantial similarity to past proposals and release a statement explaining the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indemnification of directors and officers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Association shall, to the maximum extent permitted by law, indemnify any person made or threatened to be a party to an action or proceeding by reason of being or having been a director or officer of the Association or serving at its request as a director/officer of another entity, against expenses, judgments, fines, settlements, and other amounts actually and reasonably incurred, provided the person acted in good faith for a purpose reasonably believed to be in the Association's best interests and (for criminal actions) had no reasonable cause to believe their conduct was unlawful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Association shall advance expenses to the maximum extent permitted by law. The Board may, in its discretion, by resolution provide indemnification or advances to other agents of the Association, and may refuse except where indemnification is mandatory under the N-PCL. Indemnity does not include defense for actions taken in violation of these bylaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: The fiscal year of the Association shall begin on July 1 and end on June 30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report of directors content and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall present at the annual meeting a report, verified by the president and treasurer or by a majority of the directors, or certified by an independent public or certified public accountant selected by the Board, showing in appropriate detail: assets and liabilities as of end of the fiscal period; principal changes in assets and liabilities during the period; revenue (unrestricted and restricted); expenses for general and restricted purposes; number of members as of the date and statement of increase/decrease and where names/places of residence of current members may be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This annual report shall be filed with the records and a copy or abstract entered in the minutes of the annual meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to financial statements by members
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon written request of any person who has been a member of record for at least six months immediately preceding the request, the Association shall give or send an annual balance sheet and profit and loss statement or similar financial statement for the preceding fiscal year, and the most recent interim financial statement if such an interim statement has been distributed to members or made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Association shall be allowed a reasonable time to prepare such annual or interim financial statements.
